findings.daCurrent:
• Nominativ - subject of the sentence (who does?)
  • Akkusativ - direct object (what?)
  • Dativ - indirect object (to whom?)
findings.proposedDa:
• Nominativ - sætningens grundled (hvem gør noget?)
  • Akkusativ - direkte objekt (hvad? hvem?)
  • Dativ - indirekte objekt (til hvem?)
findings.reason: The summary is partly in English and therefore not suitable for Danish learners.

findings.daCurrent: Wir mögen Euk. – Vi kan lide dig.
findings.proposedDa: Wir mögen Euch. – Vi kan lide jer.
findings.reason: Euk is a typo for Euch, and the Danish object pronoun must be jer, not dig.

findings.daCurrent: Wir danken Euk. – Vi takker.
findings.proposedDa: Wir danken Euch. – Vi takker jer.
findings.reason: Euk is a typo for Euch; the Danish translation is incomplete.

findings.daCurrent: The Nominative is always the subject of the sentence, while the Akkusativ and Dativ are the objects. Look at the verb and ask: Hvad? or Wen?
findings.proposedDa: Nominativ er altid sætningens grundled, mens Akkusativ og Dativ er objekter. Se på verbet, og spørg: Hvad? eller Hvem?
findings.reason: The note is in English and incorrectly leaves the German question word Wen in the Danish explanation.
